body: There are a small number of cases where a header needs a class to work, but wasn't including it. These things were being included transitively when 3D is enabled in the editor, but fail to compile otherwise. This PR fixes these cases by adding the includes, ~~including this one include in the core folder~~, and a few others elsewhere.

There were a few APIs in the animation editor, and this signal for communicating with `Node3DEditor`, with "transform" in the name, but these APIs only operate on 3D transform. I've renamed them with "3d" for clarity. These are internal APIs, not exposed anywhere.
When there's more than one 3D include, I separated it out.

This preserves the transform data of CanvasItems, though the data still doesn't end up being used currently. I didn't want to change too much in this PR but this would enable us to support Control nodes in `EditorNode::reload_instances_with_path_in_edited_scenes()` later if we wanted to.
This groups together EditorNode's registration of 3D material conversion plugins.
Another internal editor function which was 3D-only, but not named as such.

body: ~~In a few cases, I also grouped together physics includes. This can be used with `#ifndef PHYSICS_3D_DISABLED`, but it's also a nice organization on its own, I would argue.~~

I re-ordered the node type suffixes in `ResourceImporterScene::_pre_fix_node` to have the physics ones grouped together at the bottom. Previously the order was Physics -> Navigation -> Occluder -> Physics Again. Now the order is Occluder -> Navigation -> Physics. This doesn't change behavior as these suffixes all have unique endings.

Moved FogVolume below CanvasItem to group together 3D things (except 3D particles are still on top with 2D particles, those are required to check first because we don't want the CanvasItem check to match GPUParticles2D).
A bit noisy of a diff, but the existing empty lines made no sense, now they do.
Group together 3D editor plugin APIs.
~~Most of this PR is grouping 3D, but I also grouped 2D includes here, for symmetry with the 3D includes.~~
Several renames for clarity, and to match Godot's `p_` naming convention. `node` -> `p_node`, `rids` -> `p_col_obj_rids`, `co` -> `col_obj`, and below `rids` -> `col_obj_rids_to_exclude`.

This is using `->call("get_sprite_frames")` immediately below, so this is less code and more straightforward of a check. Technically could allow user-made AnimatedSprite classes, but that wasn't a goal here, just a happy consequence.

In these if statements, put Control-based things first, and Node2D/Node3D things after it. This is arguably more organized, but the motivation here was so you can put `#ifndef _2D_DISABLED` above the `} else if (condition) {`.
This variable is only ever null or the result of `body_create()`, so it's a body. The word "instance" is too generic, it's not clear if it's a body, area, shape, etc. Therefore, I renamed it.
Do you plan to do the same with other includes? (e.g. `gui`).

I don't want to propose that, because I don't have a clear use case that can clearly define why we would separate some of the includes from others.

The editor entirely depends on GUI, so we can't ever compile a non-GUI editor, it's a nonsense goal.
Then I don't see why 3D should be special here.

??
Doesn't Sprite2D fit here too?
I tested it and don't see any difference in behavior.

We have `editor/scene/2d/` and `editor/scene/3d/` folders, so the editor code already has a separation of 2D and 3D. Even if we never merge in the ability to compile the editor without 3D, it's still possible to do.

> Even if we never merge in the ability to compile the editor without 3D, it's still possible to do.

Yeah, but the include separation should be part of that change. Otherwise we end up with some files arbitrarily making a `// 3D` section for includes, and nothing else.

> We have editor/scene/2d/ and editor/scene/3d/ folders, so the editor code already has a separation of 2D and 3D.

When I asked about future plans, I meant any potential include grouping. Having only 3D separation is odd.
